The comparison examines the age at diagnosis for prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation across [[danmark|Danmark]] and its five administrative regions. Because the data is drawn from a single snapshot in the 2025 report, it is not possible to establish longitudinal trends or changes over time; the figures represent a static cross-section of the prevalent patient population [^src1].

Across the country, the national average age at diagnosis is 70 years, with a median of 72 years and a standard deviation of 12 [^src1]. The regional averages are highly consistent, clustering tightly between 70 and 71 years. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] share the highest average age at 71 years, while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] report an average of 70 years [^src1]. The median age is uniformly 72 years across all regions and the national total [^src1].

The total number of prevalent patients recorded nationally is 138,889 [^src1]. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] accounts for the largest regional share with 38,830 patients, whereas [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] has the smallest cohort with 14,929 patients [^src1]. 

An outlier pattern emerges in the minimum and maximum ages. While the minimum age is recorded as 0 across all regions and the national total, the maximum age varies slightly by geography [^src1]. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] report the highest maximum age at 105 years, while [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] records the lowest maximum age at 101 years [^src1]. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] fall in between with maximum ages of 103 and 104 years, respectively [^src1]. There are no unreported cases for age in any region, indicating complete data capture for this metric [^src1]. Furthermore, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] is the only region with a slightly wider age spread (standard deviation of 13) compared to the national average and other regions (standard deviation of 12) [^src1]. No specific clinical targets or thresholds are defined in this dataset to evaluate whether regions are meeting or missing standard goals.

Broader context regarding atrial fibrillation incidence, clinical guidelines, pharmacological treatments, and healthcare quality indicators is extensively detailed across the 2023, 2024, and 2025 annual reports [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19] [^src20] [^src21] [^src22] [^src23] [^src24] [^src25] [^src26] [^src27] [^src28] [^src29] [^src30] [^src31].
